science.model_version: Graphical Calculus Dimensional Operation Selection Model v1 (W = int F dx, F = -dU/dx)

self_teaching_test.learner_can_explain: A learner must explain how coordinate axis units determine whether a graph feature represents work via area or force/velocity via slope.
self_teaching_test.novice_dependency_check: A novice must understand basic dimensional analysis and calculus definitions of derivative and integral before interpreting physics graphs.
self_teaching_test.unassisted_question: On a graph of force F (N) against position x (m), a curve forms a semi-circle of radius 2 m above the axis. What physical quantity and value does the area represent?
self_teaching_test.expected_reasoning: Dimensional analysis confirms that the area under an [F vs x] graph has physical units [N] * [m] = Joules, which represents work done. For a semi-circle of radius 2 m, the area is 0.5 * pi * r^2 = 0.5 * pi * (2)^2 = 2 * pi ≈ 6.28 Joules.
self_teaching_test.counterfactual_reasoning: A novice might attempt to calculate the slope of the curve to find work, confusing the integral operator with the derivative operator and yielding dimensionally invalid units of Newtons per metre instead of Joules.

core1b.anchor_problem: A student inspects three notebook graphs: Graph A is F_x vs x (horizontal line at +3 N from 0 to 2 m); Graph B is U vs x (line from (0, 9 J) to (2 m, 3 J)); Graph C is s vs t (line from (0, 0) to (3 s, 6 m)). Determine work from Graph A, force from Graph B, and velocity from Graph C.
core1b.new_problem: A physics student analyzes three experimental cards with straight graph segments: Card R (force-position) has y-axis F_x (N) and x-axis x (m), rising linearly from (0 m, 0 N) to (4 m, 8 N). Card S (potential-position) has y-axis U (J) and x-axis x (m), rising linearly from (0 m, 2 J) to (2 m, 8 J). Card T (displacement-time) has y-axis s (m) and x-axis t (s), passing through (0 s, 0 m), (2 s, 4 m), and (5 s, 16 m). Calculate: (1) work done on Card R over 0 to 4 m, (2) conservative force component on Card S, and (3) velocity on Card T between t = 2 s and t = 5 s.
core1b.anchor_crux: Graph A (F_x vs x): Area represents work: W = (3 N) * (2 m) = +6 J. Graph B (U vs x): Slope is dU/dx
core1b.new_crux: 1. Card R (F_x vs x): Work is represented by the area under the triangular curve: W = 0.5 * base * h
core1b.numeric_swap_rejected: The anchor problem analyzes three simple horizontal lines, while the Core1B transfer presents a triangular force area, an inclined potential slope requiring the negative gradient, and a two-segment displacement-time track requiring interval slope selection.

stages.predict: Predict which of three experimental cards requires area under the curve and which require slopes.
stages.attempt: Execute area calculation on Card R, negative slope on Card S, and interval slope on Card T.
stages.reconstruct: Demonstrate that Card R work is +16 J, Card S conservative force is -3 N, and Card T velocity is 4 m/s.
stages.diagnose: Identify whether the minus sign was omitted in F_x = -dU/dx or if Card R was computed as a rectangle.
stages.repair: Recall that conservative force opposes the potential gradient (F_x = -dU/dx) and triangular area is 0.5*base*height.
stages.boundary_test: Evaluate conservative force when potential curve flattens horizontally, verifying F_x = 0 N.

hints.H1: Card R requires an area calculation (triangle: 0.5 * base * height).
hints.H2: Card S requires a slope calculation, with a negative sign because F_x = -dU/dx.
hints.H3: Card T requires the slope Delta s / Delta t over the interval from 2 s to 5 s.
